claims.text: A page exists at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ (the Pulumi docs support index links to it as the 'Provider support policy' page).
The Pulumi provider support policy page describes how long Pulumi maintains each provider major version.
Only some Pulumi providers receive long-term security updates, and the provider support policy page states which ones.
Pulumi focuses on actively supporting the latest released major version of the providers it maintains.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to a year, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The provider support policy page at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ exists and lists the covered providers and what a long-term support release contains.
Older provider major versions (beyond the covered previous major for widely used providers) receive no patches at all from Pulumi.
The Pulumi Registry at /registry/ shows the current version for all providers maintained by Pulumi.

Each major version of a Pulumi provider includes migration logic to smooth the upgrade from the immediately previous major version, but these migrations do not always work across multiple major versions.
The npm tilde operator (~1.2.3) allows patch updates on the current minor version.
Experimental features are always opt-in and can be enabled with an environment variable such as PULUMI_EXPERIMENTAL=true.
Pulumi Cloud provides built-in drift detection for automated drift detection and remediation on a schedule.
Pulumi actively maintains the latest released major version of every provider it publishes.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to 12 months, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
Pulumi provider long-term support applies to AWS, Azure Classic, Azure Native, Azure AD, Command, Docker Build, GCP, Kubernetes, TLS, and Vault providers.
Registry package pages exist at /registry/packages/ for aws, azure, azure-native, azuread, command, docker-build, gcp, kubernetes, tls, vault.

The LTS branch ships High/Critical CVE security patches, including fixes for CVEs in the provider's code or direct dependencies and fixes for broken internal infrastructure on the LTS branch needed to ship them.
An LTS release does not contain new upstream API versions, new resources or properties, performance improvements, non-security bug fixes, or compatibility with newer language runtime versions.
LTS providers remain compatible with the version of Pulumi they were frozen at unless security fixes require otherwise.
Exactly one long-term support major version exists per covered provider at any time.
When N+1 ships, N becomes the LTS major and the old LTS major reaches end of life the same day, regardless of remaining 12-month window.
Within the LTS major, only the latest minor version receives patches; earlier minors are frozen.
LTS releases are available through the same standard package registries as current-major releases but are tagged differently.
Customers pinning to a specific major version automatically receive patch releases as they ship, and pinning is recommended.
Older majors (N-2 and older) receive no patches and are end of life; if v3 is newest, v2 is N-1 and v1 and earlier are end of life.
The current major (N) receives new features, new resources, bug fixes, security patches, dependency upgrades, and new upstream API versions until N+1 ships.
Linked pages exist: FAQ anchor 'what-are-the-best-practices-for-maintaining-provider-versions', /registry/, and /docs/support/getting-support/.
